problem: Let $A$  be the set of all integers greater than $0$ and let $B$  be the set of all multiples of $3$ greater than $0.$ What is $A-B?$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding Differences of Sets Given Verbally
examples.problem: Let $A$ be the set of all multiples of $4$ that are greater than $0$ and let $B$ be the set of all multiples of $6$ that are greater than $0.$ What is $A \setminus B?$
examples.worked_solution:
The multiples of $4$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
A = \{ 4,8,12,16,20,24,28,32, 36 \ldots \}.
$$

Likewise, multiples of $6$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
B = \{ 6,12,18,24,30,36,\ldots \}.
$$

Now, $A \setminus B$ is the *difference* of $A$ and $B,$ which means that we want to find the elements that are in $A$ but *not* in $B.$

The elements of $A$ that are also in $B$ are $12, 24, 36$ and so on (i.e. multiples of $12$). So, we must remove these elements from $A.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A∖B & =A-B \\  & ={4,8,12,16,20,24,28,32,36,…}-{6,12,18,24,30,36,…} \\  & ={4,8,16,20,28,32,…}.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
The set $B∖A$ is the set of all elements belonging to $B$ but *not* $A.$ Note that no elements of $A$ are also in $B.$  Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}B∖A & =B-A \\  & ={2,4,6,8,10}-{1,3,5,7,9} \\  & ={2,4,6,8,10}.\end{aligned}
$$
